prompt.adult: Proverbs 1:6 explains what the sayings help a person understand. After “To understand a proverb and,” what does the verse name next?
prompt.child: The opening of Proverbs names what these sayings help you understand. After “a proverb and,” what does 1:6 name?
prompt.teen: Proverbs 1:6: “To understand a proverb and” what?
prompt.older: According to Proverbs 1:6, after “To understand a proverb and,” what is named?

verses.text: To understand a proverb and an enigma, The words of the wise and their riddles.

explanation.child: Look right after “a proverb and” in verse 6.
explanation.teen: 1:6 names this next, after a proverb. Read that word.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:6 also says, “The words of the wise and their riddles.”
teaching.takeaway: The sayings help a person understand a proverb and an enigma.

verses.text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, his utterance. This man declared to Ithiel—to Ithiel and Ucal:

explanation.child: Look right after “to Ithiel—” in verse 1.
explanation.teen: 30:29 names what is majestic in pace; 30:1 ends with this second name. Read that phrase.

teaching.takeaway: The man declared to Ithiel and Ucal.

prompt.adult: Proverbs 22:23 says the LORD will plead the cause of the poor. In 22:25, after warning about an angry man, what does the verse say you may set?

prompt.teen: Proverbs 22:25: “And” what, after “Lest you learn his ways”?

choices.text: And set a snare for your steps
And set a snare for your house
And set a snare for your name
And set a snare for your soul

verses.text: Lest you learn his ways And set a snare for your soul.

teaching.takeaway: And set a snare for your soul.
